simple.meaning: הֲדַס (hădaç) is a Hebrew object word meaning “the myrtle.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Nehemiah 8:15. The surrounding context includes mountain, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֲדַס (H1918) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: הֲדַס (hădaç) / H1918 is traced through Nehemiah 8:15, Isaiah 41:19, Isaiah 55:13, Zechariah 1:8 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: and that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters,”

timeline.evidenceText: and that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters,”
I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness.
Instead of the thorn the cypress tree will come up;

“I had a vision in the night, and behold,† “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. a man riding on a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in a ravine; and behind him there were red, brown, and white horses.
The man who stood among the myrtle trees answered, “They are the ones Yahweh has sent to go back and forth through the earth.”
They reported to Yahweh’s angel who stood among the myrtle trees, and said, “We have walked back and forth through the earth, and behold, all the earth is at rest and in peace.”
